BiblicalUsage: Shaashgaz is the king's chamberlain who kept the concubines, and his custody is where Esther's story turns. In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz — and she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and she were called by name.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Shaashgaz is the doorkeeper of the king's favour: the women went in once, and only the one the king delighted in and called by name came again.
